title: SEBI - 0062/2003 — Prakash Gaggar v. Securities and Exchange Board of India
text:
IN THE SECURITIES APPELLATE TRIBUNAL
MUMBAI
Appeal No. 62 of 2003
Prakash Gaggar ...... Appellant
Versus
Securities and Exchange Board of India ..…Respondent
Shri Shyam Mehta, Advocate for the appellant
Shri Kumar Desai, Advocate with Ms. Daya Gupta, Advocate for the
Respondent.
Coram: Justice N. K. Sodhi, Presiding Officer
R. N. Bhardwaj, Member
Arun Bhargava, Member
Per: Justice N. K. Sodhi, Presiding Officer (Oral)
This order will dispose of two Appeals nos.62 and 63 of 2003 both of
which are directed against two separate but identical orders dated April 2,
2003 directing the appellants to disassociate themselves from the capital
market for a period of three years and they were further prohibited from
dealing in securities for the said period. When these appeals came up for
hearing on April 13, 2006 they were disposed of as infructuous because the
period for which the appellants had been debarred had run out. Feeling
aggrieved by the fact that the appeals had not been decided on merits, the
appellants approached the Supreme Court and their Lordships by their order
dated November 6, 2006 set aside our order with a direction to hear and

.2.
dispose of the appeals on merits. This is how the appeals have come up for
hearing today. Counsel for the parties are agreed that common questions of
law and fact are involved in these appeals. Since we are remanding the case
back to the Securities and Exchange Board of India (for short ‘the Board’) it is
not necessary to state the facts in detail.
Prakash Gaggar and Suresh Gaggar are the two appellants in these
appeals and they acquired shares of Yashodham Commercial Enterprises Ltd
(hereinafter called ‘the company’) alongwith their respective Hindu Undivided
Family (HUF) and Ms. Sangeeta Gaggar. The Securities and Exchange Board
of India (Substantial Acquisition of Shares and Takeovers) Regulations, 1994
(for short ‘the Regulations’) came into force with effect from 7.11.1994. They
define the term ‘acquirer’ to mean any person who acquires or agrees to
acquire shares in a company either by himself or with any person acting in
concert with the acquirer. It is not in dispute that the two appellants had
acquired shares alongwith others acting in concert with them. It is common
ground between the parties that 64,100 shares of the company were acquired
by the appellants alongwith others and these constitute 25.8% of the total
share capital of the company. Regulation 9 of the Regulations provides that
any acquirer who holds shares carrying ten per cent or less of voting rights in
the capital of a company shall not through negotiations acquire any further
shares, which, when taken together with his existing shareholding would carry
more than ten per cent of the voting rights, unless, he makes a public
announcement to acquire shares at a minimum offer price from the other
shareholders of the company in accordance with the Regulations. The Board
in the impugned order found that the appellants acting in concert with their
HUF’s and Ms. Sangeeta Gaggar had acquired shares exceeding ten per cent

.3.
of the total share capital of the company and since they did not make a public
announcement to acquire further shares of the company they violated the
Regulations. By separate orders dated 2.4.2003 the Board debarred them from
accessing the capital market for a period of three years and also prohibited
them from dealing in securities during that period.
We have heard the learned counsel for the parties at some length. The
primary contention of the learned counsel for the appellant is that the shares
were acquired much prior to the coming into force of the Regulations and
therefore his clients were not liable to come out with a public announcement
in terms of Regulation 9(1) of the Regulations. This stand is strongly refuted
on behalf of the Board. The fact that the appellants acted in concert with
others as aforesaid while acquiring shares of the company is not disputed.
What is in issue is the date of acquisition. In order to verify the actual date of
acquisition/transfer of shares from the records of the company an
investigating team of the Board visited the registered office of the company on
27th July, 1999. Admittedly, the records pertaining to the transfer of shares
and details of transfer committee meetings were not produced before the
investigating team. Before passing the impugned order the Board afforded an
opportunity of personal hearing to the appellants on October 26, 2002. The
appellants appeared before the Board and after making verbal submissions
filed their written submissions as well on 11.11.2002 supported by documents
including copies of the share certificates purporting to contain the
endorsement transferring the shares in favour of the appellants and others
acting in concert with them. There were several other documents as well
which were sent to the Board on 20th November, 2002. It appears that the
Board looked into those documents and observed that the signatures of one of

.4.
the directors of the company Shri Kailash Bajaj on the current account
opening form of Indian Bank dated 28.10.1982 and the share transfer
certificates enclosed with the written submissions did not tally. In view of
this, the Board jumped to the conclusion that the documents submitted by the
appellants had been materially altered and were doctored documents and came
to the conclusion that the shares were transferred in the name of the appellants
and others acting in concert with them after the coming into force of the
Regulations. This finding is strenuously disputed before us on behalf of the
appellants. The documents which were submitted to the Board have also been
produced before us alongwith the memorandum of appeal. The learned
counsel for the appellant strenuously urged that the shares were actually
transferred on 24.10.1994 and in support of this plea he has relied upon the
copies of the share certificates and the share transfer deeds which prima facie
support his contention. Having gone through the impugned order we find that
the Board has not gone into the details of the documents that were produced
by the appellants to show that the shares had been acquired by them before
24.10.1994. According to the learned counsel for the appellant the material
date is the date of acquisition of shares though according to him the shares had
even been transferred prior to the coming into force of the Regulations. He
contended that the acquisition was prior to the date on which they were
transferred. This aspect of the matter has not been examined by the Board and
a finding has been recorded that the appellants (Gaggars) had acquired more
than ten per cent voting rights in the company after 31.5.1995. Great stress
was laid by learned counsel for the respondent on the signatures of the director
on the account opening form and the share transfer certificates and other
documents to contend that these documents were not genuine. We find that all

.5.
these aspects have not been properly examined by the Board and that a finding
needs to be recorded as to the precise date on which the shares were acquired
by the appellants and others acting in concert with them. May be, that the
signatures of the director on the account opening form do not tally with his
signatures on the share transfer certificates and other documents but this fact
by itself may not be sufficient to come to a finding either way. In this view of
the matter we set aside the impugned order and remand the case to the Board
with a direction to the appellants to appear before it on May 21, 2007 for
further proceedings. The appellants will be at liberty to produce further
records/documents in their possession in support of their plea. It will also be
open to the Board to summon from the appellants such further record as it may
deem necessary for deciding the aforesaid issue. After examining the
documents and the records the Board shall pass a fresh order in accordance
with law expeditiously but not later than September 30, 2007. There is no
order as to cost.
